operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The clause ended by its own terms on 1949-01-16. The order forbids any change, except by agreement, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the order's date and for thirty days after the board made its report to the President. The board's report is shown by the dated transmittal letter, December 17, 1948 (the cited end source; submission date, receipt by the President may have been later). Thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949 (14 days remain in December after the 17th, and 16 more fall in January). The end is recorded inclusive of that day, and the exclusive reading (ending when that day begins) is the alternative. The board's own commands (to investigate and to report) were performed when the report was submitted on 1948-12-17, which is not later than the standstill's end. The thirty-day report deadline is not an end. The amendment by Executive Order 10015 added carriers and renamed organizations only and did not change the thirty-day term. Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, revokes this order by number and is recorded as the later formal disposition; it is not the first end because the order's own term had already ended. No saving provision appears in it.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10010
Creating an E mergency B oard to I nves­
tigate D isputes  B etween  the A kron 
&  Barberton B elt R ailroad C ompany 
and O ther C arriers, and C ertain of 
Their  E mployees
WHEREAS disputes exist between the 
Akron &  Barberton Belt Railroad Com­
pany and certain other carriers desig­
nated in List A attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, and certain of their em­
ployees represented by the sixteen co­
operating railway labor organizations 
designated in List B attached hereto and 
made a part hereof; and 
WHEREAS these disputes have not 
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions jof the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threaten substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said disputes.
No member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of railway employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
disputes within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by any of the carriers involved or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said disputes arose.

WHEREAS Executive Order No. 589 of 
March 14,1907, recited in part that pass­
ports issued by the Government of Ja­
pan to Japanese or Korean citizens who 
were skilled or unskilled laborers to go 
to Mexico, Canada, or Hawaii 'were be­
ing used for the purpose of enabling the 
holders thereof to come to the conti­
nental territory of the United States to 
the detriment of labor conditions there­
in, and ordered that such citizens of Ja­
pan or Korea be refused permission to 
enter the continental territory of the 
United States and 
WHEREAS Executive Order No. 1712 
of February 24, 1913, recited that pass­
ports issued by certain foreign govern­
ments to their citizens or subjects, skilled 
or unskilled laborers, to go to countries 
or places other than the continental ter­
ritory of the United States were being 
used for the purpose of enabling the 
holders thereof to come to the x  conti­
nental territory of the United States to
the detriment of labor conditions there­
in, and ordered that such alien laborers, 
skilled or unskilled, be refused permis­
sion to enter the continental territory 
of the United States; and
WHEREAS the continued restraint 
imposed by the said Executive orders 
upon the freedom of Japanese or Korean 
citizens or subjects who entered the Ter­
ritory of Hawaii under the passports 
referred to above to come to the con­
tinental United States has resulted in 
considerable personal hardship to such 
persons; and
WHEREAS the number of Japanese 
or Korean citizens or subjects thus pro­
hibited from entering the continental 
United States from the Territory of Ha­
waii is so small, and the age of such 
persons is so advanced, that their entry 
into the continental United States would 
no longer be a detriment to labor con­
ditions therein:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 3 of the 
Immigration Act of 1917 (39 Stat. 875; 
8 U. S. C. 136), I hereby revoke the said 
Executive Orders No. 589 of March 14, 
1907, and No. 1712 of February 24, 1913, 
to the extent that they are applicable 
to Japanese or Korean citizens or sub­
jects who entered the Territory of Hawaii 
under the aforesaid passports and who 
are now precluded from legally enterr 
ing or remaining in the continental ter­
ritory of the United States by reason of 
such Executive orders.
The Commissioner of Immigration and 
Naturalization is hereby authorized and 
directed, with the approval of the At­
torney General, to take such action and 
to issue such rules and regulations as 
may be necessary for carrying out the 
provisions of this order.
H arry S. Truman
The W hite H ouse,
October 18, 1948.

research_rationale:
Identity. The held Federal Register text of Executive Order 10038, signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House, February 15, 1949, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Eastern Carriers' Conference Committee, Western Carriers' Conference Committee and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committee, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen. Text printed on the same Federal Register pages outside the order is not part of it. Inventory. The order is one block of text with four commands: create a three-member board, bar members from any interest in an employee organization or carrier, require the board to report within thirty days of the order, and forbid any change except by agreement in the conditions out of which the dispute arose from the order's date until thirty days after the board has made its report. I read the whole text; the one-clause inventory covers all of it and no operative sentence lies outside it. End. The last command to end is the no-change command, which by its own terms runs until thirty days after the board made its report. The report date comes from the held NMB report PDF jobs/ptolemy-custody/output/raw/eb50dfae502cd169f9ed405087972672ccd7aad5b3929edd617eca15a77d41c5.pdf (SHA-256 verified), Presidential Emergency Board report No. 70 (NMB Case A-3045), through a source excerpt of its cover page and transmittal letter. The letter is dated September 19, 1949 and says the board submits its report herewith. I also read the page image of the letter, which shows the date cleanly; the text layer of the excerpt garbles the year or lacks the line, and the cover page in the same excerpt carries the date. Thirty days after September 19, 1949 is October 19, 1949 (11 days remain in September after the 19th, and 19 more fall in October). I record the end as 1949-10-19, inclusive of that day, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21; the exclusive reading, under which the command ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The letter date is the date of submission; receipt by the President may have been later, and no held source gives a receipt date. The report's introduction records that the board could not report within the thirty days the order allowed and that extensions of the reporting time were requested through the National Mediation Board, the last to September 19, 1949; those extensions concern the due date of the report, not the thirty-day measure, which runs from the actual report. Later events. Executive Order 12553 (signed February 25, 1986, 51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986) lists this order by number in a table of orders revoked together with any amendments to them; it came 37 years after the own-terms end and is recorded as the formal disposition. Searches. The U.S. Code search (release point through 2026-10-09), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 and the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note search returned no other instrument affecting this order apart from the events recorded. Savings: none found.

research_rationale:
Identity. The held Federal Register text of Executive Order 10139, signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House, July 3, 1950, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, Local 158, A. F. of L.. Text printed on the same Federal Register pages outside the order is not part of it. Inventory. The order is one block of text with four commands: create a three-member board, bar members from any interest in an employee organization or carrier, require the board to report within thirty days of the order, and forbid any change except by agreement in the conditions out of which the dispute arose from the order's date until thirty days after the board has made its report. I read the whole text; the one-clause inventory covers all of it and no operative sentence lies outside it. End. The last command to end is the no-change command, which by its own terms runs until thirty days after the board made its report. The report date comes from the held NMB report PDF jobs/ptolemy-custody/output/raw/7e200439f16974842877b4a7398f8fec1a110094122d00e66e516fab12c6080d.pdf (SHA-256 verified), Presidential Emergency Board report Nos. 87 and 88 (joint report) (NMB case A-3380-3430), through a source excerpt of its cover page and transmittal letter. The letter is dated August 11, 1950 and says the board submits its report herewith. I also read the page image of the letter, which shows the date cleanly; the text layer of the excerpt garbles the year or lacks the line, and the cover page in the same excerpt carries the date. Thirty days after August 11, 1950 is September 10, 1950 (20 days remain in August after the 11th, and 10 more fall in September). I record the end as 1950-09-10, inclusive of that day, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21; the exclusive reading, under which the command ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The letter date is the date of submission; receipt by the President may have been later, and no held source gives a receipt date. The same held PDF is cited for Executive Orders 10138 and 10139; it is one joint report of the board appointed July 3, 1950 for both disputes (cover: boards 87 and 88, NMB case A-3380-3430), with one transmittal letter that names both the Toledo, Lorain and Fairport Dock Co. and the Toledo Lakefront Dock Co. disputes. The bytes are therefore this order's report. The report also records that the board took up further dock disputes at Cleveland and Huron by agreement; those are not disputes of this order. The report says the President extended the date of the report to not later than September 1, 1950; the report was submitted earlier, on August 11, 1950. That extension concerns the due date only. The U.S. Code search (release point through 2026-10-09), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 and the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note search returned no other instrument affecting this order apart from the events recorded. research_rationale:
Identity. The held Federal Register text of Executive Order 10147, signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House, August 4, 1950, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the New York Central Railroad Company, Lines East of Buffalo, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, the Order of Railway Conductors and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. Text printed on the same Federal Register pages outside the order is not part of it. Inventory. The order is one block of text with four commands: create a three-member board, bar members from any interest in an employee organization or carrier, require the board to report within thirty days of the order, and forbid any change except by agreement in the conditions out of which the dispute arose from the order's date until thirty days after the board has made its report. I read the whole text; the one-clause inventory covers all of it and no operative sentence lies outside it. End. The last command to end is the no-change command, which by its own terms runs until thirty days after the board made its report. The report date comes from the held NMB report PDF jobs/ptolemy-custody/output/raw/ce6afc9e9c0f8278a2f9138315f873c45a615af966021b17eae4bfc6178391e9.pdf (SHA-256 verified), Presidential Emergency Board report No. 91 (NMB Case A-3419), through a source excerpt of its cover page and transmittal letter. The letter is dated September 13, 1950 and says the board submits its report herewith. I also read the page image of the letter, which shows the date cleanly; the text layer of the excerpt garbles the year or lacks the line, and the cover page in the same excerpt carries the date. Thirty days after September 13, 1950 is October 13, 1950 (17 days remain in September after the 13th, and 13 more fall in October). I record the end as 1950-10-13, inclusive of that day, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21; the exclusive reading, under which the command ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The letter date is the date of submission; receipt by the President may have been later, and no held source gives a receipt date.  Later events. Executive Order 12553 (signed February 25, 1986, 51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986) lists this order by number in a table of orders revoked together with any amendments to them; it came 36 years after the own-terms end and is recorded as the formal disposition. Searches. The U.S. Code search (release point through 2026-10-09), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 and the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note search returned no other instrument affecting this order apart from the events recorded. Savings: none found.
